sections.heading: Introduction
sections.body: Kalymnos is a Greek island sport-climbing destination near Kos with dense limestone climbing around Massouri.

sections.heading: History and context
warnings: No sourced history and context content found for this pass.

sections.heading: Rock and climbing character
sections.body: The source mix supports solid limestone, tufas, caves, slabs, pockets, overhangs and mostly single-pitch bolted routes, with some bolted multipitch lines.

sections.heading: Who it suits
sections.body: The external route range and legacy text support both lower-grade holiday climbers and climbers seeking steep tufa routes.

sections.heading: Grades and difficulty
sections.body: Climb Europe reports about 4,200 routes from F3 slabs to F9a routes; the legacy packet reports about 64 sectors.

sections.heading: Season and conditions
sections.body: The legacy packet supports April-May and October-November, warns summer is too hot, and says winter rain can leave tufas slow to dry.

sections.heading: Gear and equipment
warnings: No sourced gear and equipment content found for this pass.

sections.heading: Transport and access
sections.body: Legacy access is by flight to Kos and ferry, or flight via Athens to Kalymnos airport.

sections.heading: Where to stay
sections.body: The legacy packet lists Masouri and Armeos with hotels, budget hotels, B&Bs and apartments.

sections.heading: Rest days
sections.body: The legacy packet mentions beaches, bars and island rest-day ambience.

sections.heading: Practical tips
warnings: No sourced practical tips content found for this pass.

sections.heading: Safety notes
sections.body: The legacy packet flags wet tufas as slow to dry, which should affect route choice after rain.
